entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Gonfalonier was the holder of a highly prestigious communal office in medieval and Renaissance Italy, notably in Florence and the Papal States.
The office of Gonfalonier was established in the 13th century, with the first recorded holder being Guido Novello da Polenta in 1274.
This position was crucial in the governance of the city-states, as the Gonfalonier played a key role in the military and administrative decisions of the commune.

The Gonfalonier was responsible for leading the city's armed forces and representing the commune in diplomatic relations with other cities and the Holy See.
They were also responsible for the administration of justice, taxation, and the management of public works.
The office was typically held by a member of the ruling family or a prominent noble.

The legacy of the Gonfalonier can be seen in the development of modern democratic institutions in Italy.
The office of the Gonfalonier was a key precursor to the modern office of the Mayor of Florence.
The Gonfalonier's role in representing the city in international relations also laid the groundwork for Italy's future role in European politics.

As the poet Matteo Maria Boiardo said, 'The Gonfalonier is the soul of the city, the heart of the commune.'
